summary: This program stores two whole numbers in variables, adds them together into a third variable, and prints the result. It is the previous PrintNumber example extended to perform a mathematical operation.

lines.text: A variable declaration names a piece of memory and gives it a value; `int` means it holds a whole number, so `a` can be used later anywhere the value 20 would work.
The `+` operator adds the two values, and the result is stored in a new variable named `sum`. Naming the result makes the intent of the calculation obvious to anyone reading the code.
Passing the variable rather than a number prints whatever `sum` currently holds, so changing the values of `a` and `b` changes the output without touching this line.

The AI might have picked different numbers, or added them directly inside `println` and skipped the `sum` variable entirely. Variations like these are fine as long as the code is clear and the result is the same.
